paper_title: What are they talking about Benchmarking Large Language Models for   Knowledge-Grounded Discussion Summarization
caption: Paragraph retrieval ratios 0.90\% of LLMs. The majority of LLMs can be classified as either conservative (ratio<300.90{%}) or open retrievers (ratio>380.90{%}).
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates paragraph retrieval ratios for an “Expert” reference and a set of large language models, with each bar representing a single system’s retrieval ratio. The category axis is the horizontal (x) axis, showing the systems in the displayed order: Expert, GPT‑4o, GPT‑4‑turbo, GPT‑4o‑mini, Claude 3 Opus, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama‑3.1‑405B, Mistral Large, DeepSeek V3, Qwen2‑Max, and GLM‑4‑Plus; the “Expert” tick label is visually emphasized in red italics while the others appear in standard dark text. The value axis is the vertical (y) axis labeled “Retrieval Ratio (%)”, using a linear scale spanning 0 to 50 with evenly spaced tick marks at 10‑point intervals. Each bar is a distinct solid color (various muted/pastel tones) and has its exact value printed above it: Expert (dark gray) 34.11, GPT‑4o (greenish) 29.07, GPT‑4‑turbo (purple) 29.16, GPT‑4o‑mini (blue) 43.57, Claude 3 Opus (mauve) 25.92, Claude 3.5 Sonnet (light blue‑gray) 31.56, Claude 3.5 Haiku (tan) 28.49, Gemini 1.5 Pro (light blue) 39.37, Llama‑3.1‑405B (lavender) 37.99, Mistral Large (beige) 31.04, DeepSeek V3 (light gray) 46.94, Qwen2‑Max (very light olive/gray) 34.84, and GLM‑4‑Plus (pale pink) 43.58; the smallest labeled bar is Claude 3 Opus at 25.92 and the tallest is DeepSeek V3 at 46.94. There is no stacking or within-category grouping, no legend, and the bars do not appear to be sorted by value.
